explanation: Searched Mathlib for a Lie-module analogue of the projection splitting lemma: grepped for `IsCompl` throughout `Mathlib/Algebra/Lie`, for `isCompl_of_proj` everywhere (only hits: `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Projection.lean`, plus uses for plain submodules in `Maschke.lean`, `Basis/VectorSpace.lean`, `Implicit.lean`), and for any statement combining `LieModuleHom`/`LieSubmodule` with `IsCompl` or invariant complements. The only Lie-theoretic `IsCompl` results are specific ones (Fitting decompositions, Cartan/coroot, Killing-complement, invariant-form orthogonal complements); none states that an equivariant projection with `ψ|_N = id` yields a complement Lie submodule. The closest Mathlib declaration is `LinearMap.isCompl_of_proj` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Projection.lean), which is about plain submodules; deriving the Lie-submodule statement from it is not a one- or two-line special case, since it requires building a `LieModuleHom M N` via `codRestrict` (packaging the equivariance hypothesis into `map_lie'`), passing between `LieSubmodule.ker` and the linear `ker`, and transporting `IsCompl` across `LieSubmodule.isCompl_toSubmodule` — more than routine glue. Hence no duplicate and no mere special case.
